neutral_facts.value: The accused was involved in a criminal case under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 477A, and 120B of the IPC, as well as Sections 13(1) and 13(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act. The Vigilance Department initiated an inquiry against the accused after a complaint was filed. The case was delayed due to a writ petition filed by the accused challenging the inquiry. The High Court directed the trial court to expedite the proceedings. However, an application was filed by a third party, who claimed to be a social activist, seeking to expedite the trial. The High Court dismissed the application, finding that the applicant had no locus standi to file such a petition. The trial court had not yet framed charges as of the date of the judgment.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that criminal trials involving offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act must be conducted and concluded at the earliest to ensure justice is delivered to the accused if found guilty.

quotes.text: It is the obligation of the State and the prosecution to ensure that all criminal trials are conducted expeditiously so that justice can be delivered to the accused if found guilty.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that the High Court erred in entertaining the application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. filed by respondent No.2, who had no locus standi to challenge the criminal proceedings.

quotes.text: The High Court committed error in entertaining the application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. at the instance of respondent No.2 who had no locus standi to file a petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the principle that criminal trials involving offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act must be expedited, and that third parties cannot raise issues under the garb of Public Interest Litigation.

quotes.text: Criminal trial where offences involved are under the Prevention of Corruption Act have to be conducted and concluded at the earliest, since the offences under Prevention of Corruption Act are offences which affect not only the accused but the entire society and administration.
